Evidence: package.json:1; scripts/check-decision-citation-drift.mjs:1-34; no tracked .bee/config.json or CI trigger

````text
scripts/check-decision-citation-drift.mjs
1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: // check-decision-citation-drift.mjs -- detects two families of citation
3: // defect across docs/backlog.md, docs/specs/*.md, and any --skills-dir
4: // roots (recursive, *.md):
5: // (1) dead-framing: a line cites a decision (ADR<n> or a bare NNNN) which
6: //     has since been superseded, without naming the superseding decision
7: //     on the same line (STR72 CoS clause 2, PBI p-2d71dfc3 -- not covered
8: //     by p-9fb81485, which checks decisions/*.md's own internal
9: //     backward-pointer pair instead).
10: // (2) citation-format (tsk-37i D3): a bare ADR<n>/RUL<n> id with no
11: //     one-line gloss immediately after it, or a D-local id (D<n>) cited
12: //     anywhere outside its own CONTEXT.md at all (decision 0017 -- a
13: //     D-local id is never cited outside its home, gloss or not; the only
14: //     correct fix is inlining the content and deleting the id).
15: //     Deliberately out of scope (tsk-37i D3, not re-opened here): a bare
16: //     4-digit id with no `ADR`/`RUL`/`D` prefix at all is not detected by
17: //     this finding type -- that is the pre-tsk-1lv-4 ADR<n>-prefix
18: //     convention, superseded by docs/decisions/index.md (generated,
19: //     tsk-1lv-2/4) now that docs/decisions/000N-*.md itself is retired; a
20: //     bare 4-digit id is only ever caught here when it cites a superseded
21: //     decision (finding (1) above already covers that case).
22: // Detection only -- flags, never fixes. Ratchets against a checked-in
23: // baseline (tsk-37i D4/D8): --write-baseline snapshots every current
24: // finding of every kind; a bare run only fails on a finding NOT already
25: // in the baseline.
26: //
27: // tsk-1lv-1 additive exports (below `runCli`): the write-time sweep
28: // `fgos decision --relation supersedes:<id>|touches:<id>` runs widens
29: // this file's own citation scan from backlog.md+specs/*.md-only to
30: // docs/**+src/**+plugins/**, for an arbitrary relation id (not only the
31: // 4-digit ADR ids `extractCitedIds` above assumes) — see
32: // `collectWideSourceFiles`/`findWideCitationFindings`. These are pure,
33: // additive, and never called by this file's own CLI mode above, so the
34: // existing backlog/specs-only default stays byte-identical.
````

### correction-18 — docs/platform/herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md

Before:
````text
It is enabled by default (its own config toggle defaults ON, unlike other auto-launch toggles), listens on the
  configured bind address (default reaches beyond loopback — binds 0.0.0.0 by default, bind address configurable, warns when non-loopback) and on port
  8788 (its config section carries a port field, defaulting to 8788).
````

After:
````text
Static serving defaults ON (`herdrWebDashboard.staticServing`); the gateway started with `fgos gateway start` listens on the
  configured bind address (default reaches beyond loopback — binds 0.0.0.0 by default, bind address configurable, warns when non-loopback) and on port
  4170 by default (`gateway.port` overrides it).
````

688: /// partial-update semantics (only fields present in the body change,
689: /// per D1 of docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard-plan-realignment/CONTEXT.md
690: /// — PATCH over PUT because PUT implies a full-resource replace this
691: /// endpoint never does). Accepts any subset of `src/state/store.mjs`'s
692: /// `EDITABLE_FIELDS` (21 entries, read directly from that file rather than
693: /// re-guessed) as a raw JSON object rather than a typed struct per field:
694: /// a field this handler does not recognize is silently dropped, mirroring
695: /// `bin/fgos.mjs`'s own `edit` case, which never errors on an unrecognized
696: /// flag either — this handler translates, it does not validate (R2 of the
697: /// area spec: validation stays at the engine, never re-implemented at a
698: /// client-facing layer; `fgos edit`'s own real rejection — including "no
699: /// field changed" — reaches the caller verbatim through the same
700: /// `run_verb_blocking`/`GatewayError` path every other write route uses).
701: async fn patch_work(
702:     State(state): State<AppState>,
703:     AxPath(id): AxPath<String>,
704:     AppJson(body): AppJson<serde_json::Map<String, Value>>,
705: ) -> Result<Json<Value>, GatewayError> {
706:     reject_leading_dash(&id, "id")?;
707:     let mut args = vec!["edit".to_string(), id];
````

Legacy authority remains unchanged; source wording is preserved for conservation, including known stale assertions.\n\n\nThe fgOS plugin lets a person working inside Claude Code operate the fgOS\nwork-item lifecycle — claim, submit, move, monitor, and inspect work — as\n`/fgOS:<verb>` slash commands, without hand-typing the underlying command-line\ntool or its arguments. Every command is a thin, safety-checked wrapper: it\nshells out to the one underlying tool, never touches the work-item store\ndirectly, and shows the real error and stops when anything goes wrong. The\nlifecycle rules each verb enforces (what \"move\" is allowed, what \"return\"\nchecks, what triggers \"awaiting-human\") are owned by the Work-State area\n(`docs/specs/work-state.md`) — this spec covers only the plugin's own\nconvenience layer on top of that."

  "sourceShownText": "## Entry Points & Triggers\n\n- `/fgOS:submit <free-text>` → intake a new work item from a plain-language description.\n- `/fgOS:pick [id]` → claim the next (or a named) work item and switch straight into its own isolated workspace.\n- `/fgOS:move <id> <status>` → move a work item to a new status.\n- `/fgOS:return <id>` → complete a claimed item: run its own verification and advance it.\n- `/fgOS:ask <id> <question text>` → park a work item pending a question, with the question attached.\n- `/fgOS:answer <id> <answer text>` → resume a parked work item once its question is answered.\n- `/fgOS:ready` → list every work item ready to be picked up right now.\n- `/fgOS:stale` → list work items that look stuck (claimed but inactive too long).\n- `/fgOS:rollup <id>` → show one work item's children: how many are done out of the total, and each child's status.\n- `/fgOS:check [id]` → show the predicted-vs-actual outcome report for one item, or every item at once.\n- `/fgOS:graph [id]` → show work-graph metrics (independent parallel tracks), or — with an id — what completing that one item would unblock.\n- `/fgOS:conflicts` → list pairs of ready work items whose declared file footprints overlap (a parallel-work collision risk).",

      "text": "- `/fgOS:submit <free-text>` → intake a new work item from a plain-language description.\n- `/fgOS:pick [id]` → claim the next (or a named) work item and switch straight into its own isolated workspace.\n- `/fgOS:move <id> <status>` → move a work item to a new status.\n- `/fgOS:return <id>` → complete a claimed item: run its own verification and advance it.\n- `/fgOS:ask <id> <question text>` → park a work item pending a question, with the question attached.\n- `/fgOS:answer <id> <answer text>` → resume a parked work item once its question is answered.\n- `/fgOS:ready` → list every work item ready to be picked up right now.\n- `/fgOS:stale` → list work items that look stuck (claimed but inactive too long).\n- `/fgOS:rollup <id>` → show one work item's children: how many are done out of the total, and each child's status.\n- `/fgOS:check [id]` → show the predicted-vs-actual outcome report for one item, or every item at once.\n- `/fgOS:graph [id]` → show work-graph metrics (independent parallel tracks), or — with an id — what completing that one item would unblock.\n- `/fgOS:conflicts` → list pairs of ready work items whose declared file footprints overlap (a parallel-work collision risk)."
    }
  },

    "text": "- `/fgOS:submit <free-text>` → intake a new work item from a plain-language description.\n- `/fgOS:pick [id]` → claim the next (or a named) work item and switch straight into its own isolated workspace.\n- `/fgOS:move <id> <status>` → move a work item to a new status.\n- `/fgOS:return <id>` → complete a claimed item: run its own verification and advance it.\n- `/fgOS:ask <id> <question text>` → park a work item pending a question, with the question attached.\n- `/fgOS:answer <id> <answer text>` → resume a parked work item once its question is answered.\n- `/fgOS:ready` → list every work item ready to be picked up right now.\n- `/fgOS:stale` → list work items that look stuck (claimed but inactive too long).\n- `/fgOS:rollup <id>` → show one work item's children: how many are done out of the total, and each child's status.\n- `/fgOS:check [id]` is not shipped; the original report description below is legacy surface documentation.\n- `/fgOS:graph [id]` → show work-graph metrics (independent parallel tracks), or — with an id — what completing that one item would unblock.\n- `/fgOS:conflicts` → list pairs of ready work items whose declared file footprints overlap (a parallel-work collision risk)."

  "sourceShownText": "## Business Rules\n\n- **R1.** The plugin wraps exactly 12 verbs total: `submit`, `pick` (existing) plus `move`, `return`, `ask`, `answer` (manipulate), `ready`, `stale`, `rollup` (monitor), `check`, `graph`, `conflicts` (inspect) — added deliberately to cover convenience for manipulating, monitoring, and inspecting work, not to mirror every command the underlying tool exposes (per 7574fe5a).\n- **R2.** Every command is one-door-write: it only ever shells out to the underlying tool's own command for that verb — it never writes the work-item store directly.\n- **R3.** On a failing command, the person sees the real error and the command stops — it never retries with a guessed argument and never falls back silently.\n- **R4 (not yet implemented — see `docs/backlog.md`).** The remaining verbs the underlying tool exposes (`init`, `add`, `discover`, `compound`, `edit`, `decision`, `list`, `rebuild`, `repair`, `take`, `review`, `approve`, `reject`, `catchup`, `evolve`, `triage`, `docs-index`, `doc-sources`, `session`) have no plugin wrapper; a person needs them must use the underlying tool directly.",

      "text": "## Business Rules",
      "sectionText": "## Business Rules\n\n- **R1.** The plugin wraps exactly 12 verbs total: `submit`, `pick` (existing) plus `move`, `return`, `ask`, `answer` (manipulate), `ready`, `stale`, `rollup` (monitor), `check`, `graph`, `conflicts` (inspect) — added deliberately to cover convenience for manipulating, monitoring, and inspecting work, not to mirror every command the underlying tool exposes (per 7574fe5a).\n- **R2.** Every command is one-door-write: it only ever shells out to the underlying tool's own command for that verb — it never writes the work-item store directly.\n- **R3.** On a failing command, the person sees the real error and the command stops — it never retries with a guessed argument and never falls back silently.\n- **R4 (not yet implemented — see `docs/backlog.md`).** The remaining verbs the underlying tool exposes (`init`, `add`, `discover`, `compound`, `edit`, `decision`, `list`, `rebuild`, `repair`, `take`, `review`, `approve`, `reject`, `catchup`, `evolve`, `triage`, `docs-index`, `doc-sources`, `session`) have no plugin wrapper; a person needs them must use the underlying tool directly."
    }

    "text": "## Business Rules\n\n- **R1.** The plugin wraps more than the original 12 verbs: shipped skills include `approve`, `list` and `triage`; `/fgOS:check` has no shipped skill, so this is a partial inventory of the shipped surface.\n- **R2.** Every command is one-door-write: it only ever shells out to the underlying tool's own command for that verb — it never writes the work-item store directly.\n- **R3.** On a failing command, the person sees the real error and the command stops — it never retries with a guessed argument and never falls back silently.\n- **R4.** Additional plugin wrappers are shipped, including `approve`, `list` and `triage`; the original remaining-verbs list is no longer a list of unimplemented wrappers."

  "sourceShownText": "# Spec: Decision Citation Drift Check\n\nA read-only detection check that scans the product backlog and area specs for\nlines that still cite a decision by its old id after that decision has been\nsuperseded, without also naming the decision that replaced it. Its purpose is\nto catch \"dead framing\" — a backlog row or spec line whose reasoning was\noverturned, but whose wording still reads as if the old decision were current,\nso a reader (human or agent) re-derives the outdated conclusion. Used by\nwhoever maintains `docs/backlog.md` and `docs/specs/*.md` (a human operator or\nan agent doing grooming/scribing).",

    "sectionText": "# Spec: Decision Citation Drift Check\n\nA read-only detection check that scans the product backlog and area specs for\nlines that still cite a decision by its old id after that decision has been\nsuperseded, without also naming the decision that replaced it. Its purpose is\nto catch \"dead framing\" — a backlog row or spec line whose reasoning was\noverturned, but whose wording still reads as if the old decision were current,\nso a reader (human or agent) re-derives the outdated conclusion.   "sourceShownText": "## Purpose\n\nThe web dashboard is a browser surface for watching fgOS work and answering\nthe questions it raises, from a device that is not the developer's machine.\n\nThe need it exists for is concrete, and it is the reason the design looks the\nway it does: the product owner wants to **review and approve from a phone**,\nand at exactly that moment there is usually no cockpit terminal open\n(rationale: `docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard/CONTEXT.md`'s own rationale section for the child-process decision — the dashboard runs as a child process that outlives the cockpit pane, precisely so it does not vanish when the terminal closes). A surface that\nonly lives as long as a terminal pane is absent precisely when it is needed.\n\nThree things bound this surface:\n\n- It runs **alongside** the herdr TUI, never replacing it (boundary: the web dashboard belongs to the fgos gateway, `apps/fgos-gateway/`; it runs alongside, not instead of, the `herdr-dashboard` TUI plugin). A\n  person at a terminal keeps the TUI; the dashboard serves the person who is\n  not at one.\n- It is an **independent client project**, not server code inside the gateway\n  (per fgos-interface-daemon — gateway and TUI sit behind hexagonal ports; the web client is a separate adapter calling in from outside). Its source lives at `apps/fgos-gateway/web/`; the fgos gateway embeds the built bundle and serves it, which is hosting, not ownership of any API logic. It calls the gateway's REST/RPC API from the outside,\n  which is what decision `0014` requires of any non-terminal UI. An earlier\n  decision of this feature (tsk-ldb's own — web dashboard as a new subsystem inside the former single herdr crate) proposed embedding an HTTP server\n  directly in the former combined gateway-and-TUI binary (since split into `fgos-gateway` and `herdr-dashboard`); that branch is closed — cite fgos-interface-daemon's hexagonal-ports decision, not\n  tsk-ldb's original one, for where the web client lives.\n- It never becomes a second write path. Every change it makes goes through\n  an fgOS one-door-write verb executed by the gateway (R2 below).\n\n**Out of scope for this spec.** Question authoring quality at the source\n(`tsk-539`, deliberately decoupled — tsk-ldb and tsk-539 stay scope-separated). Multi-project port/identity\nmechanics (`tsk-3b0` — multi-project port/identity handling is deferred to tsk-3b0). The concrete visual layout, colour and\ntypography (`tsk-3x6`, `docs/reference/herdr-web-dashboard-layout.md`) — this\nspec states what an actor expects to be able to do, never how it is drawn.",

  "sourceShownText": "## Entry Points & Triggers\n\n- **Open the dashboard.** A person opens the dashboard's address in a browser\n  on any device that can reach the machine. The first interaction is always\n  sign-in; there is no anonymous view (mandatory token auth from v1, not deferred to a later version).\n- **Open the taskboard.** The default landing surface once signed in: every\n  work item on the connected project, grouped so the person can see state at a\n  glance.\n- **Open one task's detail.** From the taskboard, or directly by address.\n- **Open \"questions needing answer\".** The list of everything currently\n  waiting on a person — covering **both** channels, `ask` questions and\n  `gate-approve` questions (question-needing-answer covers both channels), not just the `ask` channel.\n- **Availability trigger (not a person's action).** The dashboard is reachable\n  whenever its own process is running. That process is started and stopped\n  from the cockpit but **outlives the cockpit pane** — closing the cockpit does\n  not stop the dashboard (it runs as a child process outliving the cockpit pane). It is enabled by default (its own config toggle defaults ON, unlike other auto-launch toggles), listens on the\n  configured bind address (default reaches beyond loopback — binds 0.0.0.0 by default, bind address configurable, warns when non-loopback) and on port\n  8788 (its config section carries a port field, defaulting to 8788).\n- **No outbound trigger exists.** Nothing notifies the person that a question\n  is waiting; they have to come and look. A push/attention channel is a\n  different, unbuilt capability (`docs/io-contract.md` §Ranh giới — STR48).",

Static serving defaults ON (`herdrWebDashboard.staticServing`); the gateway started with `fgos gateway start` listens on the\n  configured bind address (default reaches beyond loopback — binds 0.0.0.0 by default, bind address configurable, warns when non-loopback) and on port\n  4170 by default (`gateway.port` overrides it).\n- **No outbound trigger exists.** Nothing notifies the person that a question\n  is waiting; they have to come and look.   "sourceShownText": "## Business Rules\n\n- **R1.** The surface is a client of the gateway's API, never an embedded\n  server inside the former combined binary (per fgos-interface-daemon's hexagonal-ports decision, decision `0014`). It is built to\n  address more than one gateway, so no single fixed origin may be baked into\n  it (per fgos-interface-daemon's per-machine-scope decision).\n- **R2.** Every write goes through an fgOS one-door-write verb — `answer`\n  (forwarding `--approve` when `approve: true`), `approve`, the intake verb, `edit`,\n  `move` (forwarding `--approve` when `approve: true`) — executed by the gateway, which\n  is the sole component that runs those verbs on a client's behalf (per fgos-interface-daemon — gateway is the sole chokepoint that ever spawns fgos verbs). The web surface never writes fgOS state directly. No second write path\n  is introduced by anything in this spec.\n- **R3.** A person may not read anything before signing in (mandatory token auth from v1). Sign-in is\n  token-based, and every failure is indistinguishable from \"nothing here\"\n  (an opaque 404, never 401). A second, alternative credential path exists in the design and, if\n  used, must verify its assertion's signature properly rather than trusting a\n  header (the two-layer additive auth design — cookie session plus an optional cf-access JWT that must be cryptographically verified, never trusted on the header alone).\n- **R4.** The token is never stored anywhere that is committed. It comes from\n  the environment when set; otherwise it is generated into a local file that\n  is excluded from version control and readable only by its owner.\n- **R5.** The surface is enabled by default (its own config toggle defaults ON, unlike other auto-launch toggles) and its default bind reaches\n  beyond loopback (binds 0.0.0.0 by default, bind address configurable), with a warning raised when the bind is not loopback.\n  Its port is 8788, chosen to coexist with the neighbouring service on 8787\n  (its config section carries a port field, defaulting to 8788).\n- **R6.** The dashboard's lifetime is independent of the cockpit's. Closing a\n  cockpit pane does not stop it (it runs as a child process outliving the cockpit pane).\n- **R7.** A merge approval can only be performed where fgOS allows it: the\n  `approve` verb structurally refuses to run from a linked worktree and\n  requires the repository's main working tree. This is a real mechanical\n  constraint on the deployment, not a UI concern — a gateway positioned\n  anywhere else cannot offer this operation at all, and the surface must\n  report that honestly rather than appearing to offer it.\n- **R8.** The combination of R5 (on by default, bind beyond loopback) and the\n  write operations above means **the first run of the cockpit exposes a\n  trunk-changing surface on the network, without anyone having chosen to**.\n  The token (R3/R4) is therefore not a hardening layer that can be traded away\n  for convenience — it is the only thing holding the surface closed. The\n  product owner decided this default having been shown this exact consequence\n  (rationale: `docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard/CONTEXT.md`'s own consequences section for the on-by-default decision), and the\n  write operations added later raise its weight rather than changing the\n  decision.\n- **R9.** Questions and answers are paired positionally, by order of\n  recording, with no linking key added to the underlying records — the record\n  shape is deliberately unchanged.\n- **R10.** The narrative written for humans is the primary account of what an\n  agent did; the machine-side decision log is secondary detail.\n- **R11.** Nothing on this surface pushes to a person. Being informed is a\n  pull: the person opens the dashboard and looks.",

It comes from\n  the environment when set; otherwise it is generated into a local file that\n  is excluded from version control and readable only by its owner.\n- **R5.** Static serving defaults ON (`herdrWebDashboard.staticServing`), while gateway lifecycle is controlled by `fgos gateway start`; its default bind reaches\n  beyond loopback (binds 0.0.0.0 by default, bind address configurable), with a warning raised when the bind is not loopback.\n  Its port defaults to 4170; the override is `gateway.port`.\n- **R6.** The dashboard's lifetime is independent of the cockpit's. Closing a\n  cockpit pane does not stop it (it runs as a child process outliving the cockpit pane).\n- **R7.** A merge approval can only be performed where fgOS allows it: the\n  `approve` verb structurally refuses to run from a linked worktree and\n  requires the repository's main working tree. This is a real mechanical\n  constraint on the deployment, not a UI concern — a gateway positioned\n  anywhere else cannot offer this operation at all, and the surface must\n  report that honestly rather than appearing to offer it.\n- **R8.** The combination of R5 (on by default, bind beyond loopback) and the\n  write operations above means **the first run of the cockpit exposes a\n  trunk-changing surface on the network, without anyone having chosen to**.\n  The token (R3/R4) is therefore not a hardening layer that can be traded away\n  for convenience — it is the only thing holding the surface closed. The\n  product owner decided this default having been shown this exact consequence\n  (rationale: `docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard/CONTEXT.md`'s own consequences section for the on-by-default decision), and the\n  write operations added later raise its weight rather than changing the\n  decision.\n- **R9.** Questions and answers are paired positionally, by order of\n  recording, with no linking key added to the underlying records — the record\n  shape is deliberately unchanged.\n- **R10.** The narrative written for humans is the primary account of what an\n  agent did; the machine-side decision log is secondary detail.\n- **R11.** Nothing on this surface pushes to a person. Being informed is a\n  pull: the person opens the dashboard and looks."
  },

There is no per-person, per-project, or per-verb distinction to\n  spec against, because neither fgOS nor the gateway has one (STR38 unbuilt;\n  fgos-interface-daemon's own one-token-per-machine decision does not add one). The exposure is stated rather than mitigated. Closing this\n  needs its own item and its own decision — the authorization layer's own\n  scope, not this spec's, and not something to be improvised inside the web\n  client.\n- **The gateway's own API contract now exists** —\n  `docs/contracts/fgos-gateway-api-v1.yaml`, landed by tsk-7l9, carrying 18\n  paths that match `apps/fgos-gateway/src/gateway.rs`'s registered routes 1-to-1.\n  This spec still describes operations in product terms rather than\n  restating endpoint shapes, but that contract — not this prose — is the\n  boundary's source of truth, and any surface built against it cites it\n  directly.       "text": "- **Authorization granularity for write actions — unresolved, and it is the\n  significant one.** Everything under Behaviors & Operations that writes, and\n  `approve` above all, is available to whoever holds the machine's single\n  token. Ratchets against a checked-in\n23: // baseline (tsk-37i D4/D8): --write-baseline snapshots every current\n24: // finding of every kind; a bare run only fails on a finding NOT already\n25: // in the baseline.\n26: //\n27: // tsk-1lv-1 additive exports (below `runCli`): the write-time sweep\n28: // `fgos decision --relation supersedes:<id>|touches:<id>` runs widens\n29: // this file's own citation scan from backlog.md+specs/*.md-only to\n30: // docs/**+src/**+plugins/**, for an arbitrary relation id (not only the\n31: // 4-digit ADR ids `extractCitedIds` above assumes) — see\n32: // `collectWideSourceFiles`/`findWideCitationFindings`. These are pure,\n33: // additive, and never called by this file's own CLI mode above, so the\n34: // existing backlog/specs-only default stays byte-identical."
        }
      ]
    }

  "before": "## Entry Points & Triggers\n\n- **Open the dashboard.** A person opens the dashboard's address in a browser\n  on any device that can reach the machine. The first interaction is always\n  sign-in; there is no anonymous view (mandatory token auth from v1, not deferred to a later version).\n- **Open the taskboard.** The default landing surface once signed in: every\n  work item on the connected project, grouped so the person can see state at a\n  glance.\n- **Open one task's detail.** From the taskboard, or directly by address.\n- **Open \"questions needing answer\".** The list of everything currently\n  waiting on a person — covering **both** channels, `ask` questions and\n  `gate-approve` questions (question-needing-answer covers both channels), not just the `ask` channel.\n- **Availability trigger (not a person's action).** The dashboard is reachable\n  whenever its own process is running. That process is started and stopped\n  from the cockpit but **outlives the cockpit pane** — closing the cockpit does\n  not stop the dashboard (it runs as a child process outliving the cockpit pane). It is enabled by default (its own config toggle defaults ON, unlike other auto-launch toggles), listens on the\n  configured bind address (default reaches beyond loopback — binds 0.0.0.0 by default, bind address configurable, warns when non-loopback) and on port\n  8788 (its config section carries a port field, defaulting to 8788).\n- **No outbound trigger exists.** Nothing notifies the person that a question\n  is waiting; they have to come and look. A push/attention channel is a\n  different, unbuilt capability (`docs/io-contract.md` §Ranh giới — STR48).",

  "before": "## Business Rules\n\n- **R1.** The surface is a client of the gateway's API, never an embedded\n  server inside the former combined binary (per fgos-interface-daemon's hexagonal-ports decision, decision `0014`). It is built to\n  address more than one gateway, so no single fixed origin may be baked into\n  it (per fgos-interface-daemon's per-machine-scope decision).\n- **R2.** Every write goes through an fgOS one-door-write verb — `answer`\n  (forwarding `--approve` when `approve: true`), `approve`, the intake verb, `edit`,\n  `move` (forwarding `--approve` when `approve: true`) — executed by the gateway, which\n  is the sole component that runs those verbs on a client's behalf (per fgos-interface-daemon — gateway is the sole chokepoint that ever spawns fgos verbs). The web surface never writes fgOS state directly. No second write path\n  is introduced by anything in this spec.\n- **R3.** A person may not read anything before signing in (mandatory token auth from v1). Sign-in is\n  token-based, and every failure is indistinguishable from \"nothing here\"\n  (an opaque 404, never 401). A second, alternative credential path exists in the design and, if\n  used, must verify its assertion's signature properly rather than trusting a\n  header (the two-layer additive auth design — cookie session plus an optional cf-access JWT that must be cryptographically verified, never trusted on the header alone).\n- **R4.** The token is never stored anywhere that is committed. It comes from\n  the environment when set; otherwise it is generated into a local file that\n  is excluded from version control and readable only by its owner.\n- **R5.** The surface is enabled by default (its own config toggle defaults ON, unlike other auto-launch toggles) and its default bind reaches\n  beyond loopback (binds 0.0.0.0 by default, bind address configurable), with a warning raised when the bind is not loopback.\n  Its port is 8788, chosen to coexist with the neighbouring service on 8787\n  (its config section carries a port field, defaulting to 8788).\n- **R6.** The dashboard's lifetime is independent of the cockpit's. Closing a\n  cockpit pane does not stop it (it runs as a child process outliving the cockpit pane).\n- **R7.** A merge approval can only be performed where fgOS allows it: the\n  `approve` verb structurally refuses to run from a linked worktree and\n  requires the repository's main working tree. This is a real mechanical\n  constraint on the deployment, not a UI concern — a gateway positioned\n  anywhere else cannot offer this operation at all, and the surface must\n  report that honestly rather than appearing to offer it.\n- **R8.** The combination of R5 (on by default, bind beyond loopback) and the\n  write operations above means **the first run of the cockpit exposes a\n  trunk-changing surface on the network, without anyone having chosen to**.\n  The token (R3/R4) is therefore not a hardening layer that can be traded away\n  for convenience — it is the only thing holding the surface closed. The\n  product owner decided this default having been shown this exact consequence\n  (rationale: `docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard/CONTEXT.md`'s own consequences section for the on-by-default decision), and the\n  write operations added later raise its weight rather than changing the\n  decision.\n- **R9.** Questions and answers are paired positionally, by order of\n  recording, with no linking key added to the underlying records — the record\n  shape is deliberately unchanged.\n- **R10.** The narrative written for humans is the primary account of what an\n  agent did; the machine-side decision log is secondary detail.\n- **R11.** Nothing on this surface pushes to a person. Being informed is a\n  pull: the person opens the dashboard and looks.",

The web surface never writes fgOS state directly. No second write path\n  is introduced by anything in this spec.\n- **R3.** A person may not read anything before signing in (mandatory token auth from v1). A second, alternative credential path exists in the design and, if\n  used, must verify its assertion's signature properly rather than trusting a\n  header (the two-layer additive auth design — cookie session plus an optional cf-access JWT that must be cryptographically verified, never trusted on the header alone).\n- **R4.** The token is never stored anywhere that is committed. It comes from\n  the environment when set; otherwise it is generated into a local file that\n  is excluded from version control and readable only by its owner.\n- **R5.** Static serving defaults ON (`herdrWebDashboard.staticServing`), while gateway lifecycle is controlled by `fgos gateway start`; its default bind reaches\n  beyond loopback (binds 0.0.0.0 by default, bind address configurable), with a warning raised when the bind is not loopback.\n  Its port defaults to 4170; the override is `gateway.port`.\n- **R6.** The dashboard's lifetime is independent of the cockpit's. Closing a\n  cockpit pane does not stop it (it runs as a child process outliving the cockpit pane).\n- **R7.** A merge approval can only be performed where fgOS allows it: the\n  `approve` verb structurally refuses to run from a linked worktree and\n  requires the repository's main working tree. This is a real mechanical\n  constraint on the deployment, not a UI concern — a gateway positioned\n  anywhere else cannot offer this operation at all, and the surface must\n  report that honestly rather than appearing to offer it.\n- **R8.** The combination of R5 (on by default, bind beyond loopback) and the\n  write operations above means **the first run of the cockpit exposes a\n  trunk-changing surface on the network, without anyone having chosen to**.\n  The token (R3/R4) is therefore not a hardening layer that can be traded away\n  for convenience — it is the only thing holding the surface closed.         "text": "- **R1.** The surface is a client of the gateway's API, never an embedded\n  server inside the former combined binary (per fgos-interface-daemon's hexagonal-ports decision, decision `0014`). It is built to\n  address more than one gateway, so no single fixed origin may be baked into\n  it (per fgos-interface-daemon's per-machine-scope decision).\n- **R2.** Every write goes through an fgOS one-door-write verb — `answer`,\n  `approve`, the intake verb, `edit`, `move` — executed by the gateway, which\n  is the sole component that runs those verbs on a client's behalf (per fgos-interface-daemon — gateway is the sole chokepoint that ever spawns fgos verbs). The web surface never writes fgOS state directly. No second write path\n  is introduced by anything in this spec.\n- **R3.** A person may not read anything before signing in (mandatory token auth from v1). Sign-in is\n  token-based, and every failure is indistinguishable from \"nothing here\"\n  (an opaque 404, never 401). A second, alternative credential path exists in the design and, if\n  used, must verify its assertion's signature properly rather than trusting a\n  header (the two-layer additive auth design — cookie session plus an optional cf-access JWT that must be cryptographically verified, never trusted on the header alone).\n- **R4.** The token is never stored anywhere that is committed. It comes from\n  the environment when set; otherwise it is generated into a local file that\n  is excluded from version control and readable only by its owner.\n- **R5.** The surface is enabled by default (its own config toggle defaults ON, unlike other auto-launch toggles) and its default bind reaches\n  beyond loopback (binds 0.0.0.0 by default, bind address configurable), with a warning raised when the bind is not loopback.\n  Its port is 8788, chosen to coexist with the neighbouring service on 8787\n  (its config section carries a port field, defaulting to 8788).\n- **R6.** The dashboard's lifetime is independent of the cockpit's. Closing a\n  cockpit pane does not stop it (it runs as a child process outliving the cockpit pane).\n- **R7.** A merge approval can only be performed where fgOS allows it: the\n  `approve` verb structurally refuses to run from a linked worktree and\n  requires the repository's main working tree. This is a real mechanical\n  constraint on the deployment, not a UI concern — a gateway positioned\n  anywhere else cannot offer this operation at all, and the surface must\n  report that honestly rather than appearing to offer it.\n- **R8.** The combination of R5 (on by default, bind beyond loopback) and the\n  write operations above means **the first run of the cockpit exposes a\n  trunk-changing surface on the network, without anyone having chosen to**.\n  The token (R3/R4) is therefore not a hardening layer that can be traded away\n  for convenience — it is the only thing holding the surface closed. The\n  product owner decided this default having been shown this exact consequence\n  (rationale: `docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard/CONTEXT.md`'s own consequences section for the on-by-default decision), and the\n  write operations added later raise its weight rather than changing the\n  decision.\n- **R9.** Questions and answers are paired positionally, by order of\n  recording, with no linking key added to the underlying records — the record\n  shape is deliberately unchanged.\n- **R10.** The narrative written for humans is the primary account of what an\n  agent did; the machine-side decision log is secondary detail.\n- **R11.** Nothing on this surface pushes to a person. Being informed is a\n  pull: the person opens the dashboard and looks."

    "shownText": "### D-ADR0037 (Observe Component Architecture)\n\n- **Một component Observe**: Gom toàn bộ đo lường (`fgos metrics`) và friction (`fgos friction`) vào một crate Rust duy nhất (`packages/observe/rust`).\n- **Subject tầng nền**: Subject đo lường là các thực thể tầng nền (`run`, `session`, `executor`, `case`); Work Item là source quan sát tuỳ chọn, không phải trung tâm đo lường.\n- **Friction rời Work**: Lưu trữ friction tách rời khỏi `work.friction` trong Work event store; chuyển thành append-only shards trong `.fgos/observe/friction/<writerId>.jsonl`.\n- **Writer Rust duy nhất**: Mọi component ghi friction hoặc metrics đều gọi qua native CLI của Rust host. Recursion guard chỉ còn cho `legacy-cli`.\n- **`nativeOnly`**: Các verb `metrics` và `friction` được đánh dấu `nativeOnly: true` trong command registry, Node legacy CLI từ chối trực tiếp với exit 4.\n- **Không backward compat**: Supersede luật \"Preserve current commands\" của `node-to-rust-migration.md` đối với `check/faults/dispatch-report/evolve`; chuyển hẳn sang `metrics` và `friction`.\n- **Single path**: Một con đường thực thi duy nhất qua host router native.\n- **Store Observe tracked, shard theo writer**: Lưu trữ dưới `.fgos/observe/<store>/<writerId>.jsonl` được git theo dõi; migration theo cursor `(src, seq)`.\n- **Kênh phụ best-effort cho friction**: Ghi friction là kênh phụ không chặn luồng chính (lỗi ghi được ghi nhận thành `friction-write-failed` trong `invocation-faults`). Resolve host theo thứ tự ưu tiên: env (`FGOS_HOST_BIN`) → release manifest (`.fgos/installation`) → fault.\n- **Work ngừng đọc friction**: Work không đọc friction; CLI friction của Observe không join state của Work.\n- **Bỏ `learning.frictions`**: Bỏ `learning.frictions` khỏi event đóng item và bỏ mục `frictions` khỏi output của `list` / `show`.\n- **Map output `check` và `evolve`**: Outcomes, settlement, learning, nag → `metrics outcomes`; entropy → `metrics entropy`; `evolve --submit` → `friction rank` + `fgos submit`.\n",

          "line": 1093,
          "text": "- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần \"each door carries one posture lane\" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; \"an agent executor declares no `for`\" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute <id> --for <capability>` with a \"must declare\" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor.<id>.agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities.<name>.prefer`). The CLI door `execute <agent>` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute <agent> --for <capability>` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract <file> --executor <id>` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs \"this provider if it can, else any\". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run \"<prompt>\" --provider <id>` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider.",

          "text": "**Vai mù thật sự (`blind`) — chặn đọc run state của peer.** Mặc định tắt (không đổi hành vi). Một cờ ở Unit (và ở `template` của Workflow): `blind: true` làm *mọi vai* của Unit chạy với `hostRead: blind` (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` §9.2): worker không đọc được `.fgos/assignments`, `.fgos/workflow-runs`, `.fgos/dispatch-runs` của project, thư mục socket herdr, private home của dispatch khác, hay `/proc/<pid>` của tiến trình anh em; chỉ đọc được thư mục của chính nó (brief, ref đã được trao — chỉ-đọc) và ghi outbox. Phần còn lại của host (repo, `node`, DNS) và file tracked trong `.fgos` không đổi. Unit `blind` không bao giờ chạy không-blind: nếu không thực thi được — `bind()` không chọn in-process/inline, không có bwrap, mode không `required`, probe hỏng/chưa tươi, `cwd` hay ref nằm trong vùng bị che — dispatch bị từ chối trước khi spawn với lý do có tên (`blind-in-process`, `blind-requires-confinement`, `blind-hides-workspace`, `blind-ref-hidden`, `confinement-probe-failed`, ...). Với Unit `blind`, input `unit-run:`/`gate-answer:` (và ref bất kỳ nằm trong vùng bị che) không được giao bằng đường dẫn gốc: lúc dispatch, `resolveUnitInputs` + `copyHandoffsInto` chép nguyên byte (kiểm sha256) vào `inputs/` của round dir của chính vai đó, mỗi vai một bản, tên trung tính khi có `anonymizeInputs`; `unit.json` giữ `inputMap`, resume dùng lại bản chép. `blind-ref-hidden` chỉ còn cho ref không chép được.           "text": "A Unit (or Workflow unit template) with `blind: true` runs every role with `hostRead: blind`: the worker cannot read a peer's run state (`.fgos/assignments`, `.fgos/workflow-runs`, `.fgos/dispatch-runs`), the herdr socket directory, another dispatch's private home or process list. Inputs that live in the hidden run state (`unit-run:` and `gate-answer:` inputs, a panel synthesizer's panelist reports) reach each blind role as byte-identical copies in `inputs/` of its own assignment directory, neutral names (`seat-A`) with `anonymizeInputs`; a source that changed since it settled refuses the unit.           "text": "- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần \"each door carries one posture lane\" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; \"an agent executor declares no `for`\" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute <id> --for <capability>` with a \"must declare\" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor.<id>.agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities.<name>.prefer`). The CLI door `execute <agent>` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute <agent> --for <capability>` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract <file> --executor <id>` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs \"this provider if it can, else any\".           "text": "**Vai mù thật sự (`blind`) — chặn đọc run state của peer.** Mặc định tắt (không đổi hành vi).
